stories.headline: Two dead after road traffic collision in Co Donegal Gardaí are appealing for witnesses after two people died in a road traffic collision in Co Donegal this afternoon.
stories.summary: A road traffic collision in Co Donegal, Ireland, resulted in the deaths of two people. The incident occurred on the N15 at Birchhill, shortly after 2pm. Gardaí are appealing for witnesses to contact them. In a separate incident in St Johnston, two 18-year-old men, Daniel Cullen and Caoimhin Porter, died after their car collided with a lorry on Tuesday night. Gardaí continue to investigate and appeal for witnesses. The accidents are part of a series of fatal road crashes in Counties Cork and Donegal, which also claimed the lives of a motorcyclist in his 20s and a woman in her 80s. Gardaí and emergency services are working to determine the circumstances surrounding the collisions. Investigations are ongoing, and authorities are seeking information from anyone who may have witnessed the incidents.

stories.headline: Man ploughs car into crowd in Italy before trying to stab them Seven people were injured, two seriously, before passers-by gave chase and stopped the man.
stories.summary: A man drove his car into a crowd of pedestrians in Modena, Italy, injuring seven people, two of them seriously. After the incident, the driver attempted to stab the injured individuals. Passers-by intervened, giving chase and stopping the man. The attack occurred on the main shopping street of Modena, with the car smashing into a group of people and a shop window. The injured were taken for medical treatment, with two in serious condition. The driver's motives are not yet clear, and an investigation is underway. The quick response of bystanders helped to prevent further harm and apprehend the suspect. The incident has left eight people injured, with four initially reported to be in critical condition, although the latest update confirms seven injuries, with two serious cases.

stories.headline: Italy: 8 injured after driver crashes car into pedestrians in Modena Europe News: At least eight people were injured on Saturday after a car drove into pedestrians in the centre of the northern Italian city of Modena.
stories.summary: A car drove into pedestrians in the center of Modena, Italy, injuring at least eight people, four of whom are in serious condition. The incident occurred on one of the city's main streets, where the vehicle entered the sidewalk and sent several people flying before crashing into a shop window. The driver, a 30-year-old man of North African origin born in Bergamo, was arrested shortly after the incident. Authorities have stated that there is no further danger to the public. The driver attempted to flee the scene before being detained by police. The injured individuals are being treated, with four in critical condition. The incident is currently under investigation, and police have confirmed that the situation is under control.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV: the Pope of Peace Pope Leo has made peace the defining message of his pontificate, calling the world to reconciliation, dialogue, and a “disarming peace."
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has made peace the central theme of his pontificate, calling for reconciliation, dialogue, and a "disarming peace." In his first year, he has appealed hundreds of times for unarmed and disarming reconciliation, urging world leaders to listen to a higher purpose. The Pope's message emphasizes human dignity and unity, navigating global conflict and polarization. He defines the "peace of the Risen Christ" as a humble and persevering disarmed peace, distinct from the silence of weapons that comes from a ceasefire. Pope Leo's consistent call for peace has established him as a steady spiritual leader, shaping a papacy centered on unity, listening, and reconciliation amidst global turbulence. His vision of peace has been a recurring theme, with the phrase "unarmed and disarming" capturing the essence of his message.

stories.headline: Steam Machine price leak has fans excited and nervous as release date looms
stories.summary: A recent leak suggests the Steam Machine's price may be higher than expected, potentially exceeding $1,000. The leak is based on a source code update, which also hints at an imminent release date. The high price point has left some fans nervous, although it's possible the cost includes a bundle with a Steam Controller or the Frame VR headset. Previous rumors had indicated a more reasonable price tag, but the latest information has sparked concern among potential buyers. With Valve's 2026 deadline looming, fans are eagerly awaiting official confirmation of the Steam Machine's price and release date. The company has not yet commented on the leak, leaving fans to speculate about the console's cost and features. The uncertainty has generated a mix of excitement and anxiety among Steam Machine enthusiasts.

stories.headline: The special Vespera II X edition is now $341 off
stories.summary: The Vaonis Vespera II X edition is currently discounted by $341. This limited edition telescope features a unique housing design reminiscent of a sci-fi movie, making it suitable for both outdoor and indoor use. With only 300 units available, sales are already underway. The Vespera II X edition boasts a strong astrophotography capability and comes with a hard protective case and a tall carbon-fiber tripod. Vaonis has also released new models, the Vespera III and Vespera Pro 2, which offer sharper images and upgraded features for stargazing. The Vespera II X edition's discount provides an opportunity to purchase a high-end telescope at a reduced price. The Vespera series is known for its advanced technology and sleek design, making it a popular choice among astronomy enthusiasts. The discount is available for a limited time, and interested buyers can take advantage of the offer.

stories.headline: Google's new Gmail upgrade has annoyed users — here's why
stories.summary: Google has released its biggest upgrade to Gmail, introducing AI personalization features that raise privacy concerns. The update adds powerful AI tools to the inbox, processing email data off-device, even when users opt for passkeys for security. This has sparked concerns among millions of users worldwide. The Gemini integration is a key part of the upgrade, but users are advised to review their smart settings before opting in. Google's decision to push users towards AI upgrades has been met with overwhelming decisions, prompting the company to encourage users to understand the implications and adjust their settings accordingly. The upgrade affects users in the US and globally, highlighting the need for awareness about data privacy and security in the context of AI-powered email services. Users can change their settings to address these concerns.

stories.headline: PlayStation Plus Trick Secures You Early Access To May's Free Game Line-Up
stories.summary: Sony has revealed the PlayStation Plus game lineup for May, with Red Dead Redemption 2 and Star Wars Outlaws headlining the additions. The new games will become playable on May 19. However, subscribers can already claim the PlayStation Plus Essential free games for May, which include EA Sports FC 26, Wuchang: Fallen Feathers, and Nine Sols. These games were made available on May 5 and can be claimed until June 2. The PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for May also includes other titles, such as Time Crisis, which will be added to the Premium tier. The full lineup offers a range of games, including open-world experiences, and is set to become available to subscribers on May 19, although some titles are already accessible.

stories.headline: 'I can't lie' - Antoine Semenyo revels in sublime FA Cup final winner as Man City star says Pep Guardiola gives him freedom to 'create chaos'
stories.summary: Manchester City won the FA Cup for the eighth time, defeating Chelsea in the final. Antoine Semenyo scored the winning goal, a superb strike that decided a hard-fought match with few clear chances. Chelsea played a significant role in the game and felt they should have been awarded at least one penalty for a foul by Abdukodir Khusanov. Semenyo's goal was the difference-maker, and he credited manager Pep Guardiola with giving him the freedom to "create chaos" on the field. Guardiola's tactical approach allows Semenyo to be a wild card, and his goal proved decisive in the FA Cup final. The win marked a significant achievement for Manchester City, and Semenyo's goal will be remembered as a highlight of the tournament. The match was closely contested, with both teams creating limited scoring opportunities.

stories.headline: Max Ojomoh plays with magic England are missing as Henry Arundell scores four Bath 69 Newcastle Red Bulls 12: Centre discarded by Steve Borthwick at international level needs only a few minutes to steal show on return from injury
stories.summary: Bath Rugby defeated Newcastle Red Bulls 69-12 at the Recreation Ground in Round 16 of the 2025/26 Gallagher Premiership. Henry Arundell scored four tries, helping Bath end a three-match losing streak and reaffirm their second-place position. The win secured a top-four spot and closed the gap on league leaders Northampton to four points. Max Ojomoh made a notable impact on his return from injury, showcasing his skills and potentially reminding England of his abilities after being discarded by Steve Borthwick at the international level. Ojomoh's performance was a highlight in an otherwise one-sided match, with Bath dominating Newcastle throughout. The victory marked a significant turnaround for Bath, who had struggled in recent matches.

stories.headline: Premier League grounds are full now but VAR will soon make football unwatchable More delays are feared as video assistant referees will be able to get involved in corner-kick awards and second yellow cards at this summer's World Cup
stories.summary: The Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system will be expanded at the upcoming World Cup to include reviews of corner-kick awards and second yellow cards. This change, approved by the International Football Association Board (Ifab) in February, will allow VAR to intervene in these situations. However, the new law is discretionary, and leagues can choose to opt out. The Premier League is expected to decline the use of VAR for corner kicks, citing concerns about further delays and potential broadcaster dissatisfaction. A recent VAR delay in a West Ham-Arsenal match, which lasted four minutes, has sparked debate about the effectiveness of the technology. The expansion of VAR's role has raised concerns about increased disruptions to the game, with some calling for a review of the personnel operating the system.

stories.headline: 'He changed how I see football' - Bernardo Silva praises Pep Guardiola impact as Man City legend responds to uncertainty surrounding coach's future
stories.summary: Bernardo Silva has praised Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, stating that he "changed the way I see football." Silva's comments come after City's 1-0 FA Cup win over Chelsea, and ahead of his own departure from the club this summer. Guardiola's decision to let Silva leave has been met with a professional response from the player, who has chosen not to comment on the manager's future. Guardiola's impact on Silva's career has been significant, with the player crediting him with altering his perspective on the game. Silva's departure from City is expected to be a significant loss, with Guardiola's own future at the club also uncertain. Despite this, Silva has maintained a positive tone, focusing on the influence Guardiola has had on his career and the team's success.

stories.headline: India rejects Court of Arbitration’s pondage award on Indus Waters Treaty
stories.summary: India rejected the Court of Arbitration's award on maximum pondage under the Indus Waters Treaty, issued on May 15, 2026. The government stated it does not recognize the panel, calling it illegitimate. The award, issued by the Court of Arbitration at The Hague, pertains to the treaty's provisions on water sharing between India and Pakistan. India has dismissed the court's constitution, declaring the award null and void. The rejection comes as the latest development in the long-standing dispute between the two countries over the Indus Waters Treaty, which governs the sharing of water resources from the Indus River and its tributaries. The Indian government's stance is that the Court of Arbitration was illegally constituted, rendering its decisions invalid.

stories.headline: Netherlands returns 1,000-year-old Indian heritage to PM Modi
stories.summary: The Netherlands has returned 1,000-year-old Indian heritage to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The returned items include copper plates from the Chola dynasty, a significant part of India's cultural history. The Chola dynasty ruled southern India between the 3rd and 13th centuries. The copper plates are a valuable artifact, holding importance for India's historical and cultural heritage. The return of these items took place during PM Modi's visit, marking a significant moment in the preservation of India's ancient history. The gesture by the Netherlands is seen as a step towards strengthening cultural ties between the two countries. The returned artifacts will be preserved and showcased in India, allowing the public to learn about and appreciate the country's rich cultural heritage.

stories.headline: AIMPLB says HC verdict in Bhojshala case to be challenged in Supreme Court
stories.summary: The All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB) plans to challenge the Madhya Pradesh High Court's verdict in the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula dispute in the Supreme Court. The High Court recently ruled that the site is a Hindu temple, granting full worship rights to Hindus. The decision has sparked reactions from both sides, with Hindu groups celebrating and the Muslim community planning to appeal. The dispute has been ongoing, and the case may now head to the Supreme Court for further adjudication. The AIMPLB's decision to challenge the verdict comes amid heightened security in Dhar, where the site is located. The Supreme Court's decision will be crucial in resolving the long-standing dispute over the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula site.

stories.headline: NEET-UG paper leak: Doctors’ body moves Supreme Court to make NTA a statutory body accountable to Parliament
stories.summary: A doctors' body has moved the Supreme Court to make the National Testing Agency (NTA) a statutory body accountable to Parliament. The plea follows the leak of the NEET-UG 2026 paper, which was conducted on May 3, with over 22.7 lakh aspirants appearing for the exam. The doctors' body alleges a "systemic failure" in the conduct of the examination, citing the recurring issue of paper leaks, including a similar incident in 2024. The plea seeks a fresh NEET-UG 2026 exam under judicial supervision and asks the government to constitute or restructure the NTA through a statutory framework enacted by Parliament, as it currently functions under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. The petition aims to address the NTA's accountability and transparency issues.

stories.headline: The bond market is flashing a warning, energy geopolitics expert warns Daleep Singh knows how energy and markets intersect. He sees trouble ahead.
stories.summary: Concerns about energy-driven inflation have prompted a sell-off in some long-term government bonds, worrying market experts. Daleep Singh, an energy geopolitics expert, warns of trouble ahead, noting the intersection of energy and markets. He argues that the US economic power should not be guided by brute force. The bond market sell-off is a warning sign, as investors become increasingly concerned about inflation driven by energy prices. This situation has prompted some experts to sound the alarm, citing the potential for economic instability. Singh's expertise in energy geopolitics provides insight into the complex relationships between energy, markets, and economic power, highlighting the need for careful consideration of these factors to navigate the current economic landscape. His warnings suggest that the situation bears close monitoring to mitigate potential risks.

stories.headline: Energy Diplomacy in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Will Algorithms Replace OPEC? The end of traditional energy politics
stories.summary: The influence of algorithms on energy diplomacy is growing, potentially rivaling traditional institutions like OPEC. As artificial intelligence (AI) takes a leading role, energy demands are increasing, with AI data centers consuming large amounts of electricity. The development of AI is now constrained by raw energy availability, rather than algorithms or talent. The shift towards AI-powered energy systems raises questions about the future of traditional energy politics. With fossil fuels and critical non-renewables expected to be exhausted before 2100, the need for sustainable energy solutions is becoming increasingly urgent. As the energy landscape evolves, the role of algorithms and AI in shaping energy diplomacy and policy is likely to continue growing, potentially transforming the way energy is produced, consumed, and managed. This transformation may ultimately lead to a new era in energy politics.

stories.headline: Arctic Alliances: The New Front in Global Geopolitics In light of geopolitical tensions in the Arctic, Canada and Nordic countries are strengthening military and diplomatic ties.
stories.summary: Canada and Nordic countries are strengthening military and diplomatic ties in response to growing geopolitical tensions in the Arctic. The move is part of an effort to strengthen alliances between "middle powers" in a world where global tensions are rising. Canadian Prime Minister, not Mark Carney, but presumably the current leader, is leading the initiative. Recent geopolitical shifts in the Arctic have prompted the formation of stronger alliances, driven by the opening of new shipping routes due to melting ice and increasing competition. Russia has expanded its presence in the region, contributing to the pressure. Canada's collaboration with the Nordics aims to enhance Arctic defense and security, reflecting the growing importance of the region in global geopolitics. The alliances are seen as a strategic response to the changing dynamics in the Arctic.

stories.headline: Nifty Prediction For May 18: Volatility Ahead Amid Costlier Crude, Weaker Rupee; Know Support & Resistance Levels Nifty Prediction For Monday, May 18: Experts say markets are expected to remain volatile and intensely headline-driven as investors watch geopolitics and oil ma
stories.summary: Indian markets are expected to remain volatile on May 18 due to costlier crude oil and a weaker rupee. Experts predict that investors will closely watch geopolitics and oil markets, driving volatility. The rise in Brent crude oil prices to near $115 has increased inflation risk and pressure on the Indian economy. A weaker rupee has also led to investors selling Indian assets. Technically, the markets appear weak, but a bounce back is possible. Key factors driving the markets include FII selling pressure, a weak rupee, rising crude oil prices, and mixed global cues. The banking sector is expected to be weak, while other sectors may be affected by the overall market sentiment. Investors will be watching support and resistance levels to navigate the volatile market.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty outlook for Monday, May 18: What to expect from stock market
stories.summary: Domestic equity markets ended the week on a negative note, with the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty declining 2.70% and 2.20%, respectively, snapping a two-week winning streak. Looking ahead to Monday, May 18, market experts predict volatility and intense headline-driven trading. Investors will be closely watching geopolitical developments and oil prices, which are expected to influence market trends. The Sensex and Nifty are likely to remain sensitive to global cues, and traders should be prepared for potential fluctuations. With no major domestic events scheduled, global market sentiment and economic indicators will be key drivers of market movement on Monday. Investors are advised to exercise caution and stay informed about global developments that may impact the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: Nifty Breaks Down from 23,800–24,500 Consolidation Range, Weakening Market Structure
stories.summary: Nifty has broken down from its 23,800-24,500 consolidation range, indicating a weakening market structure. The index was trading near 24,100 and moving sideways, awaiting a breakout or breakdown. Technical analysts had suggested a consolidation phase rather than a reversal, with key support zones expected to hold. However, the breakdown below the range suggests a potential fall towards 23,200 levels. The 20-day exponential moving average (DEMA) had also indicated a possible fall towards 23,800-23,750 if the Nifty 50 sustained below it. The current market sentiment is weak, influenced by global factors, and the breakdown may lead to further decline in the Nifty. The next key support levels will be crucial in determining the market's direction.

stories.headline: Indian Stock Market Plunges as Global Cues Turn Bearish, Investors Lose Hope
stories.summary: The Indian stock market plunged due to weak global cues, with investors losing Rs 16.77 lakh crore. A sharp rise in US bond yields, driven by rising Middle East tensions, made equity markets less attractive, prompting investors to take profits. The Indian rupee fell to a record low, crossing the 91 mark against the US dollar, and has lost 1% in the last five trading sessions. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have been persistent sellers throughout January, and the market's sustainability depends on them flipping to net buyers. Despite starting Thursday's session in the green, the market remains under pressure due to global cues and a weak rupee. The losses mark a third straight session of decline, with investors seeking relief from recent volatility. Global trends had briefly lifted market sentiment, but overall, the market remains bearish.

stories.headline: BSE Sensex Falls Over 200 Points, Nifty Below 23,500 as Selling Pressure Intensifies
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex fell over 200 points, with the Nifty dropping below 23,500, as selling pressure intensified. This decline follows a recent trend of market volatility, with the Sensex witnessing a mildly positive session just four days ago, closing at 74,608. However, the market has since experienced significant drops, including a 1,000-point crash on March 18 and a 750-point fall on March 15. The Nifty 50 has also slipped below 23,600, with broad-based selling across sectors, led by IT. Higher crude prices, with Brent crossing $106 per barrel, have raised concerns about currency pressure and rising costs for oil-dependent sectors, contributing to the market's downward trend. The ongoing selling pressure has resulted in the Nifty falling below 23,500, indicating continued market uncertainty.

stories.headline: Weighing YONEX (TSE:7906) Valuation After Recent Share Price Weakness And Conflicting P/E And DCF Signals
stories.summary: YONEX (TSE:7906) has experienced recent share price weakness, with a 10% decline over the past month, despite being up over 60% year-to-date. The stock's long-term performance shows a modest total return over the past year, but stronger returns over the 3 and 5 year periods. A surge earlier in the year was followed by a 5.93% decline due to margin pressures from aggressive marketing and direct-to-consumer investments. Despite 18.4% sales growth and record profits, rising SGA costs have raised concerns about growth sustainability. However, a DCF analysis suggests the stock may be undervalued, with a potential 20%+ valuation gap, and a fair value of ¥4,211.7 compared to the current price of ¥3,250. This discrepancy prompts further investigation into the stock's potential upside.

stories.headline: Assessing Daikin Industries (TSE:6367) Valuation After Strong Recent Share Price Momentum
stories.summary: Daikin Industries Ltd (TSE:6367) has seen significant share price momentum, with a 1-month return of 25.28% and positive total returns over the past year and multiple-year periods. The company has also reported revenue and net income growth. Recent trading has been strong, with the stock showing gains over the past week, month, and 3 months. The current price of 20,490 is above the 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages, indicating a bullish trend. The sentiment for JP:6367 is positive, driven by the company's financial performance and share price movement. Investors are evaluating the stock's valuation and momentum to make informed investment decisions. With a strong price trend, Daikin Industries Ltd is drawing attention from investors, who are monitoring its stock price, valuation, dividends, and financials to guide their investment choices.

stories.headline: Why Nissan Motor (TSE:7201) Is Up 8.5% After Forecasting Profit Return Despite Latest Annual Loss
stories.summary: Nissan Motor Co., Ltd. reported a net loss of ¥533.10 billion for the full year ending March 31, 2026, with sales of ¥10,689.89 billion. Despite the loss, the company's shares rose 8.5% after it forecasted a return to profit. The loss per share narrowed to ¥152.58 from ¥187.08 year on year. Nissan attributed the expected turnaround to cost savings and new models. The company's stock has shown small gains over the past month, but remains negative over the past three months and year to date. The upbeat outlook has drawn fresh attention to the stock, with investors monitoring its progress. Nissan's forecast suggests a potential inflection point for the company, with investors awaiting further developments to inform their trading and investment decisions. The stock's performance will be closely watched in the coming months.

stories.headline: A Look At LeMaitre Vascular (LMAT) Valuation After Strong Q1 Results And Raised Full Year Guidance
stories.summary: LeMaitre Vascular (LMAT) reported strong Q1 2026 results, with sales of $66.6 million, an 11% increase, and organic growth of 10%. Gross margin was 72.7%, a 350 basis point increase, and operating income was $17.8 million, a 41% increase. Following the earnings beat, analysts have upgraded their earnings forecasts and raised price targets. The company also raised its full-year guidance, reinforcing positive sentiment. LeMaitre Vascular's valuation is currently at a P/E non-GAAP of 32.44, with revenue growth of 13.27% year-over-year. The company's gross profit margin and EPS growth of 42% have contributed to the positive outlook. Eight analysts have made upward revisions to their FY1 estimates, reflecting the strong Q1 performance and raised full-year outlook.

stories.headline: OpenAI Is Offering ChatGPT Plus To Citizens Of Malta For A Year Residents will have to go through a course on artificial intelligence before activating the subscription.
stories.summary: OpenAI is offering ChatGPT Plus to citizens of Malta for a year. To activate the subscription, residents must complete a course on artificial intelligence. Additionally, they need to have an active eID account from the European Union. The programme is set to start in May, and upon completing the free AI literacy course, residents will receive a full year of the premium service. This initiative aims to provide Maltese residents with access to advanced AI technology, promoting digital literacy and awareness. The course is a prerequisite to ensure users understand how to effectively utilize the ChatGPT Plus service. By completing the course, residents can unlock a year's worth of premium features and benefits. The offer is available to all residents of Malta, making it a unique opportunity for the island nation's citizens.

stories.headline: Musk-OpenAI Trial Nears High-Stakes Verdict A federal jury in California is preparing to deliberate in Elon Musk’s high-stakes lawsuit against OpenAI, a case that could reshape the future of the artificia
stories.summary: A federal jury in California is set to deliberate in Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, a case that could impact the future of artificial intelligence. Musk's lawsuit, seeking $150 billion, claims OpenAI strayed from its non-profit mission and enriched itself. The trial, which began on April 28th in Oakland, California, has seen sharp accusations exchanged between Musk and OpenAI. During closing arguments, Musk's lawyer questioned OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's credibility, accusing the company of prioritizing profits over its original mission. The jury's verdict will have significant implications for the development and regulation of artificial intelligence. The trial has been expedited, with both parties agreeing to a speedy resolution. The outcome is highly anticipated, given the high stakes and the potential impact on the tech industry.

stories.headline: OpenAI partners with Malta to give nationwide access to ChatGPT Plus US artificial intelligence company OpenAI reportedly said on Saturday that it had concluded a partnership with the Maltese government, marking a significant mov
stories.summary: OpenAI has partnered with the Maltese government to provide nationwide access to its ChatGPT Plus service. The partnership, a world's first, will give all Maltese citizens and residents free access to the service for one year. To qualify, individuals must complete a university-backed AI literacy course on responsible usage, which will start in May. The programme aims to promote AI literacy and responsible usage among the population. The government of Malta and OpenAI have announced the partnership, with official remarks highlighting the significance of the move. The initiative is expected to roll out in May, with access also available to Maltese citizens living abroad. The one-year access to ChatGPT Plus will be granted upon completion of the required course, marking a significant step in promoting AI adoption and digital literacy in Malta.

stories.headline: OpenAI seals deal in Malta to give all Maltese access to ChatGPT Plus Malta is set to become the first nation to provide all its residents with a year of ChatGPT Plus access.
stories.summary: OpenAI has signed a deal with the Maltese government to provide all residents with a year of access to ChatGPT Plus. This makes Malta the first nation to offer its entire population access to the AI service. The initiative follows the launch of Malta's Artificial Intelligence strategy, which aims to introduce AI into various aspects of Maltese life. To receive the free access, residents must complete an AI training course. The partnership is a significant step in Malta's efforts to integrate AI into its society. With this deal, all Maltese residents will be able to utilize ChatGPT Plus for a year, marking a unique collaboration between a government and an AI company. The move is expected to enhance the country's digital landscape and promote AI adoption among its citizens.
